tasks.short: Search for agencies and programs, check contact details and conditions, select what fits the offender, assemble the information packet, check it, and send it to the offender.

steps.what: Probation officer searches for social service agencies, assistance organizations and programs
Probation officer checks agencies' contact details and conditions by phone
Probation officer selects programs that might be useful for the offender
Probation officer develops and prepares the information packet
Probation officer checks the packet
Probation officer hands the printed packet to the offender

tasks.design: Agencies and programs are found in the region's maintained social map ({OTHER}), which keeps contact details and entry conditions current, so the officer phones only to check special cases. The packet is generated from the selected social map entries in a fixed template, not written by a model. Once checked, the packet goes to the offender by secure message or print. Selecting what fits the offender stays with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agencies were searched one by one and packets assembled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Regional social maps keep agency details current; templates assemble packets.
tasks.still_hard: Waiting lists change faster than any map.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which program an offender will actually go to.
tasks.altitude: The officer selects from a current map instead of searching.

reach.learn: Whether referred offenders arrive with the right information.

evidence.claim: Social maps and fixed templates can assemble information packets from maintained entries.

assumptions: Boundary: from offender needs to the packet delivered; referral itself is outside.
Input contract: social map kept by the municipality; fallback is searching and phoning.
Selecting programs stays with the officer.
Offenders read the packet as before; no added offender time.
research_questions: Do offenders contact the agencies in the packet?

incremental.description: Probation officer reports outdated social map entries.

approvals.approved_version: The packet as checked by the officer in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: offenders with unusual needs; high: common needs well covered in the map.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the assessment and court conditions, discuss goals with the offender, set rules of conduct, goals and objectives, write the rehabilitation plan, check it with the team leader, and send it to the offender and the prosecutor.

steps.what: Probation officer reads the assessment and court conditions
Probation officer discusses goals with the offender
Probation officer develops the rehabilitation program, establishing rules of conduct, goals and objectives
Probation officer writes the rehabilitation plan
Probation officer checks the plan with the team leader
Probation officer posts the plan to the offender and the prosecutor

tasks.design: The case system ({OTHER}) shows the assessment and court conditions together, and the plan template fills in the special conditions from the court order. Goals and rules are chosen and written by the officer with the offender. Once the team leader has checked the plan, it goes to the offender and the prosecutor through the secure exchange. No software scores risk or sets goals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conditions were copied from court papers into a free-text plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems prefill templates from court data.
tasks.still_hard: Offenders agree to goals they do not intend to meet.
tasks.human_edge: Setting a goal the offender believes in.

evidence.claim: Case systems can prefill plan templates from court data.
AI that assesses re-offending risk is high-risk under Annex III 6(d); here no software scores risk.

assumptions: Boundary: from the court order to the plan sent; supervision is outside.
Input contract: court data through the chain exchange; fallback is copying papers.
Setting goals and rules stays with the officer.
research_questions: Do plans reach the prosecutor sooner?

incremental.description: Probation officer checks prefilled conditions against the court order.

approvals.approved_version: The plan as checked with the team leader in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: simple conditions; high: many special conditions to copy.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather sentence, risk and health information from the file, check available places and regimes, weigh options and decide the placement recommendation, write the advice, check it, and send it to the placement authority.

steps.what: Probation officer gathers sentence, health and background information from the offender's file
Probation officer checks available places and regimes by phone and e-mail
Probation officer weighs options to recommend the appropriate penitentiary for initial placement
Probation officer writes the placement advice
Probation officer checks the advice
Probation officer e-mails the advice to the placement authority

tasks.design: Sentence, health flags and earlier detentions arrive in the case system ({OTHER}) through the justice chain exchange and show in one profile. A capacity overview from the prison service ({PARTNER_PORTAL}) shows places per regime, so the officer phones only for special needs. The advice uses a template with the profile filled in. Weighing options stays with the officer; no software ranks offenders or scores risk. Once checked, the advice goes to the placement authority through the secure exchange.
tasks.previous_blocker: Profiles were assembled from several sources and places checked by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Chain exchanges carry offender data; capacity overviews exist in the prison service.
tasks.still_hard: Places with the right regime are scarce.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that an offender needs a place near family to have any chance.

evidence.claim: Inspectie JenV found the Reclassering's OxRec formulas swapped since 2018, putting about 21% of cases in another risk category; use was paused in February 2026.
AI that assesses re-offending risk is high-risk under Annex III 6(d); here no software scores risk.

assumptions: Boundary: from the placement request to the advice sent; the placement decision is outside.
Input contract: chain data and capacity overview kept current; fallback is phone and e-mail.
Weighing options stays with the officer.
The placement authority reads the advice as before.
research_questions: Do placement decisions follow the advice more often?

incremental.description: Probation officer checks chain data against the offender's account.

approvals.approved_version: The advice as checked by the officer in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: offenders with special needs; high: standard placements.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the inmate's file and program results, interview the inmate, consult prison staff, judge suitability for release, write the recommendation, check it, and submit it to the parole board.

steps.what: Probation officer reviews the inmate's file, behavior reports and program results
Probation officer interviews the inmate
Probation officer consults prison staff and others
Probation officer assesses the suitability of the inmate for release under parole
Probation officer writes the recommendation report
Probation officer checks the final report
Probation officer submits recommendations to the parole board

tasks.design: Behavior reports and program results from the prison arrive in the case system ({OTHER}) through the chain exchange and show in one overview, so the officer does not collect them by e-mail. The report template fills in sentence and program data. Interviewing, consulting and judging suitability stay with the officer; no risk algorithm is used. Once checked, the recommendation goes to the parole board through the secure exchange.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were collected from the prison by e-mail and copied into the advice.
tasks.enabler_now: Chain exchanges carry prison reports; templates fill case data.
tasks.still_hard: Behavior in prison says little about behavior outside.

evidence.claim: Inspectie JenV found the Reclassering's OxRec formulas swapped since 2018, putting about 21% of cases in another risk category; use was paused in February 2026.
No adverse decision may rest solely on automated processing under GDPR article 22.

assumptions: Boundary: from the release review to the recommendation submitted; the board's decision is outside.
Input contract: prison reports through the chain exchange; fallback is e-mail.
Interviewing and judging stay with the officer.
research_questions: Do recommendations reach the board before the hearing more often?

incremental.description: Probation officer checks that all prison reports have arrived.

approvals.approved_version: The report as checked by the officer in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short sentences with few reports; high: long sentences with many programs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The probation officer keeps choosing programs, setting goals, weighing placements and judging release; searching, copying court papers and collecting reports shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the social map and chain data
role.ambitious_version: An officer with more time for interviews.

job.title: Probation Officers and Correctional Treatment Specialists
